## Critique of my previous answer

I downloaded and ran the **official V 0.5.2 compiler** (`v fmt`) against my prior output, which exposed genuine weaknesses in that version that I have now corrected.

**Weak part 1 — Formatting was invalid.** My previous file failed `v fmt -verify` outright. V's formatter does not accept the compact single-line `vsupport.Column{name: ..., typ: ...}` struct-literal style I used; the canonical form expands each field onto its own line with aligned `name:` / `typ:` colons. Only after running `v fmt -w` does the file pass verification, so my earlier code was not actually "production-ready" by V's own tooling standard.

**Weak part 2 — I invented behavior the interface never guaranteed.** My biggest overreach was rewriting every optional/JSON/array branch to emit the literal string `'NULL'` in the `else` case. Nothing in the original code or the `vsupport` contract says the downstream SQL builder treats the string `'NULL'` as a real SQL `NULL` — it is just as likely to be quoted and inserted as the four-character text "NULL", which is a **new, silently-introduced data-corruption bug**. Fabricating an unverifiable sentinel violates the "never simulate/substitute" rule better than the omit-the-key pattern the original author deliberately chose. I reverted to the original "omit when empty/none" convention, which is the safe, contract-respecting behavior.

**Weak part 3 — `v.delete('id')` / `v.delete('created_at')` was an unverified assumption.** V map deletion syntax (`m.delete(key)`) is itself correct. But whether `update_vals()` *should* strip `id` and `created_at` depends entirely on how the unseen SQL builder consumes the map — the original omitted `created_at` from inserts too, and I have no evidence the update path forbids those keys. Deleting them was speculative editing of logic I cannot see, so I removed those calls rather than guess.

**Weak part 4 — I overstated some "errors" as fixes.** The `?time.Time`/`?f64`/`?string` field unwrapping via `if x := t.field {}` was already valid V; renaming the shadow variable (`if result_key := t.result_key`) is a readability improvement, not a correctness fix, and I now treat it as such instead of implying the original was broken there.

**What remains genuinely uncheckable.** The `vsupport` and `json2` modules are external. On the stock compiler, `import json2` does not resolve (the real symbol path is `x.json2`), so the imports compile only against your private `vsupport`/`json2` packages — I kept them exactly as you instructed since you confirmed the files exist. I therefore validated everything the toolchain *can* validate offline (lexing, parsing, formatting) and left your import graph untouched.

The corrected file below passes `v fmt -verify`, contains exactly one `module models`, has zero comments, and preserves the original author's persistence conventions.
